materials.title: Passive Voice — be + past participle
contentText:
In a normal sentence, the subject does the action: "The director films the scene." In a passive sentence, we put the thing that receives the action first: "The scene is filmed." You do not have to say who does the action.

How to form it: [thing] + is/are + the -ed/-en form of the verb. This -ed/-en form is the past participle — the same form you already know from regular verbs in the simple past: film → filmed, produce → produced, edit → edited.

Use is for one thing, are for more than one thing:
"The show is broadcast every week."
"The scenes are edited by the director."

If you want to say who does the action, add by: "The scene is filmed by the director."

German note: In German you say "Der Film wird gedreht" — with werden. In English, use be (is/are), NOT become. Do not say: "The film becomes filmed." Say: "The film is filmed."
The show is produced in Berlin.
The scenes are edited by the director.
The news is broadcast every evening.
The documentary is filmed in London.
